stories.headline: Assam: TAIPA protests for flood compensation, preservation of monuments
stories.title: Assam: TAIPA protests for flood compensation, preservation of monuments
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAZIRA: The Tai Ahom Yuba Parishad, Assam (TAIPA), staged a sit-in protest in front of the Nazira Co-District Commissioner’s office on Tuesday, demanding adequate compensation and rehabilitation for people affected by the devastating July 19 floods, along with preservation and beautification of historical monuments across Nazira co-district.

The protest was organised by the Nazira Sub-Divisional Committee of TAIPA, in association with the Tai Ahom Mahila Parishad, Assam, following a call by TAIPA central committee President Diganta Tamuli, who was also present at the programme.
At the conclusion of the protest, memoranda were submitted separately to the Assam Chief Minister and the Nazira Co-District Commissioner through the Co-District Commissioner’s office.
Among its major demands, TAIPA called for a CBI investigation into the July 19 flood, alleging that illegal stone and coal mining may have contributed to the disaster.

It also demanded immediate payment of adequate compensation to flood victims, rehabilitation of affected families, and a special package of at least Rs 5,000 crore from the Central and State governments for rehabilitation and infrastructure development in Sivasagar district.
The organisation also demanded an inquiry into alleged irregularities in the distribution of the Rs 15,000 one-time assistance and immediate payment to all eligible families who have been left out.

article_sentences: New Delhi: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other INDIA bloc leaders were detained by police from the Akashvani Bhawan here on Tuesday, after over nine hours of staging a sit-in at the premises near the ECI's office.
However, they were released latter.

Earlier in the day, INDIA bloc MPs tried to push open the gates of the Akashvani Bhawan as they intensified their protest against the Election Commission of India (ECI), demanding Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
Holding tricolours and banners reading 'Save democracy', the INDIA bloc MPs on Tuesday commenced their protest march from Parliament to the ECI headquarters.
The Opposition leaders raised slogans against the CEC, the BJP and the RSS as they marched towards the ECI headquarters.
In view of the protest, Delhi.
Police and other security forces had been placed on alert.
Barricades were also set up outside the ECI office.
Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, along with several other INDIA bloc leaders, were also detained briefly during the day after being stopped from heading towards the ECI's office.
Gandhi was stopped by several layers of police barricades while attempting to proceed towards the ECI headquarters.
He subsequently climbed onto one of the barricades and waved a large national flag, drawing loud slogans of support from the INDIA bloc leaders and workers gathered at the spot.

Speaking to reporters from within the premises of the All India Radio (AIR) headquarters earlier on Tuesday, he said around 300 MPs from both Houses of Parliament were stopped from meeting the Election Commission.

stories.headline: US, Israel must abandon path of confrontation: Dr Farooq Abdullah
stories.title: US, Israel must abandon path of confrontation: Dr Farooq Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 6: The Jammu and Kashmir National Conference President, Dr Farooq Abdullah, Tuesday expressed deep concern over the ongoing crisis in West Asia, saying that the conflict has engulfed not only the region but has also had repercussions across the world. He appealed to all peace-loving countries, particularly Arab and Muslim nations, to utilise all available diplomatic and political avenues to help bring the present crisis to an end. "International institutions, including the United Nations and the International Court of Justice, should also play an effective role in facilitating reconciliation, dialogue and negotiations between the parties so that the region can be saved from further destruction. At the same time, Israel must be held accountable for alleged war crimes and genocide in Palestine," he said. Dr Farooq, as per a party statement, said that the United States and Israel must abandon their war-driven approach and make the protection of civilians and their lives and property their foremost priority. “War can never provide a permanent solution to any problem, and the use of force only aggravates the humanitarian tragedy,” he said. He also expressed deep regret over missile attacks by Houthi rebels towards the Holy cities of Makkah and Madinah. He said targeting or threatening the sacred places with any form of attack was deeply regrettable and had hurt the sentiments of Muslims across the world. He urged the Houthi leadership to refrain completely from such actions.

article_sentences: New Delhi: The Central government on Tuesday cleared the appointment of Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit as the next Chief of the Air Staff.
Ashutosh Dixit will take charge as the nation's 29th Indian Air Force Chief on October 31, with his tenure lasting until December 31, 2028.
Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is presently serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff.

"With the approval of the President, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM has been appointed as the next Chief of the Air Staff in the substantive rank of Air Chief Marshal, with effect from the afternoon of 31st October, 2026, with a tenure up to 31st December, 2028," said a government notification.
Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit will succeed incumbent Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh, who superannuates on October 31, 2026.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal: The hard part begins
stories.title: India-US trade deal: The hard part begins
stories.summary: India and the US are likely to eventually conclude an interim trade agreement, but a near-term breakthrough looks unlikely as the two sides remain divided over market access, agriculture, Russian oil purchases and Washington’s concerns over the bilateral trade deficit, a unit of Fitch, BMI said.The assessment comes after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on October 1 that negotiators had identified the full set of sticking points, while Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on October 5 that the talks had reached a “plateau” beyond which further concessions would be difficult.Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau, with little room left to give or take, says Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman“This confirms our February view that the announced deal was a framework rather than a completed agreement,” BMI said.The two countries have narrowed their differences, but the issues that remain are also the most politically and commercially sensitive.India is seeking meaningful preferential access for its exports, while Washington wants greater access to the Indian market, particularly in agriculture, larger purchases of US goods and a reduction in the bilateral trade deficit.Agriculture remains the biggest domestic hurdleAgriculture is likely to be among the most difficult areas for India to compromise on. The framework announced in February had identified possible concessions on animal feed, tree nuts, fruit, soybean oil, wine and spirits.India could potentially offer limited access in these segments, BMI said, but opening up dairy and genetically modified agricultural markets would carry substantially greater political costs.“India will resist costly concessions unless the US offers it a clear advantage over competing exporters,” BMI said.India’s effective tariff rate on US goods is currently 13.6%, according to BMI’s Operational Risk team, significantly below the roughly 35% starting point used in February. This means the direct gains from an interim agreement could be limited unless the deal provides preferential access in commercially important sectors.Washington is also looking for steps to narrow the bilateral goods deficit. The US recorded a $45.7 billion goods trade deficit with India in 2024.India could help reduce the gap through larger purchases of US aircraft, energy, technology and defence equipment. But such purchases would not by themselves address broader US concerns over access to the Indian market.Russian oil adds another complicationIndia’s continued dependence on Russian crude has added another layer of difficulty to the negotiations. The February framework appeared to link tariff relief with a reduction in Russian oil purchases. But the subsequent Iran conflict, which disrupted Gulf supplies, has increased India’s incentive to retain alternative sources of crude.Russia accounted for around 50.8% of India’s crude import volumes in July 2026, according to BMI.The US has also increased pressure on countries buying Russian energy after President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on September 18.Also Read: Explainer: Why have India-US trade talks stalled again and what's next?The law authorises measures linked to Russian energy purchases, including additional tariffs of up to 100% on qualifying purchasers, although waiver provisions give the US administration considerable discretion.The legislation will take effect within 30 days of its enactment, making its implementation a key factor for the trade negotiations in the coming weeks.“Whether Washington targets India, grants a waiver or uses the threat to seek trade concessions will show whether Russian oil remains negotiable or becomes a firm barrier to an agreement,” BMI said.Narrow deal could leave bigger issues unresolvedDespite the hurdles, BMI believes an interim agreement remains possible because both sides can postpone some of their most difficult disagreements.India could lower tariffs on selected US agricultural and industrial products and commit to larger purchases, while Washington could provide preferential treatment to selected Indian exports.Issues such as dairy, genetically modified products and some regulatory barriers could then be left for subsequent negotiations.India is also unlikely to permanently abandon Russian oil, BMI said. A more realistic arrangement could involve greater diversification of supplies or lower purchases from Russia when market conditions allow.For India, the biggest immediate benefit of a deal would therefore be reduced uncertainty rather than a sharp increase in exports.“A settlement would improve visibility for exporters and investors and reduce the risk of renewed tariff escalation,” BMI said, while adding that its direct trade impact would probably be modest given the current tariff rate and likely narrow product coverage.A deal would also not remove all tariff risks. India remains subject to a US Section 301 investigation into structural manufacturing overcapacity, covering sectors including petrochemicals, steel and solar modules. The USTR has not yet announced a date for its next decision.

opening: India and the US are likely to eventually conclude an interim trade agreement, but a near-term breakthrough looks unlikely as the two sides remain divided over market access, agriculture, Russian oil purchases and Washington’s concerns over the bilateral trade deficit, a unit of Fitch, BMI said.

The assessment comes after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on October 1 that negotiators had identified the full set of sticking points, while Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on October 5 that the talks had reached a “plateau” beyond which further concessions would be difficult.
body: “This confirms our February view that the announced deal was a framework rather than a completed agreement,” BMI said.
The two countries have narrowed their differences, but the issues that remain are also the most politically and commercially sensitive.

India is seeking meaningful preferential access for its exports, while Washington wants greater access to the Indian market, particularly in agriculture, larger purchases of US goods and a reduction in the bilateral trade deficit.
Agriculture remains the biggest domestic hurdleAgriculture is likely to be among the most difficult areas for India to compromise on.
The framework announced in February had identified possible concessions on animal feed, tree nuts, fruit, soybean oil, wine and spirits.
India could potentially offer limited access in these segments, BMI said, but opening up dairy and genetically modified agricultural markets would carry substantially greater political costs.
“India will resist costly concessions unless the US offers it a clear advantage over competing exporters,” BMI said.
India’s effective tariff rate on US goods is currently 13.6%, according to BMI’s Operational Risk team, significantly below the roughly 35% starting point used in February.
This means the direct gains from an interim agreement could be limited unless the deal provides preferential access in commercially important sectors.
Washington is also looking for steps to narrow the bilateral goods deficit.
The US recorded a $45.7 billion goods trade deficit with India in 2024.
India could help reduce the gap through larger purchases of US aircraft, energy, technology and defence equipment.
But such purchases would not by themselves address broader US concerns over access to the Indian market.
Russian oil adds another complication.
India’s continued dependence on Russian crude has added another layer of difficulty to the negotiations.
The February framework appeared to link tariff relief with a reduction in Russian oil purchases.
But the subsequent Iran conflict, which disrupted Gulf supplies, has increased India’s incentive to retain alternative sources of crude.
The US has also increased pressure on countries buying Russian energy after President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on September 18.
“Whether Washington targets India, grants a waiver or uses the threat to seek trade concessions will show whether Russian oil remains negotiable or becomes a firm barrier to an agreement,” BMI said.
Narrow deal could leave bigger issues unresolved.
Despite the hurdles, BMI believes an interim agreement remains possible because both sides can postpone some of their most difficult disagreements.
India could lower tariffs on selected US agricultural and industrial products and commit to larger purchases, while Washington could provide preferential treatment to selected Indian exports.
Issues such as dairy, genetically modified products and some regulatory barriers could then be left for subsequent negotiations.
India is also unlikely to permanently abandon Russian oil, BMI said.
A more realistic arrangement could involve greater diversification of supplies or lower purchases from Russia when market conditions allow.
For India, the biggest immediate benefit of a deal would therefore be reduced uncertainty rather than a sharp increase in exports.

“A settlement would improve visibility for exporters and investors and reduce the risk of renewed tariff escalation,” BMI said, while adding that its direct trade impact would probably be modest given the current tariff rate and likely narrow product coverage.
A deal would also not remove all tariff risks.
India remains subject to a US Section 301 investigation into structural manufacturing overcapacity, covering sectors including petrochemicals, steel and solar modules.
The USTR has not yet announced a date for its next decision.

sentences.text: India’s effective tariff rate on US goods is currently 13.6%, according to BMI’s Operational Risk team, significantly below the roughly 35% starting point used in February.
The framework announced in February had identified possible concessions on animal feed, tree nuts, fruit, soybean oil, wine and spirits.

The assessment comes after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said on October 1 that negotiators had identified the full set of sticking points, while Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on October 5 that the talks had reached a “plateau” beyond which further concessions would be difficult.
The US has also increased pressure on countries buying Russian energy after President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on September 18.

stories.headline: Inox Green Completes ₹550 Cr Acquisition of WWIL’s 4.5 GW Wind O&M Business
stories.title: Inox Green Completes ₹550 Cr Acquisition of WWIL’s 4.5 GW Wind O&M Business
stories.summary: Inox Green Energy Solutions Limited (Inox Green), part of the INOXGFL Group, has completed the ₹550-crore payment to acquire Wind World India Limited’s (WWIL) wind O&M business. In a press release, Inox Green, a listed renewable energy operations and maintenance (O&M) service provider, said it made the payment under a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) through its subsidiary Vibhav Energy Pvt Ltd (VEPL). Under the agreement, WWIL’s O&M business will be transferred to VEPL as a going concern. As per the terms of the BTA and the Resolution Plan approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Inox Green will hold a 75% stake in VEPL after the business transfer and implementation of the Resolution Plan is completed. This will enable Inox Green to consolidate the transferred business’s financials on a line-by-line basis. Supported by the broader INOXGFL Group ecosystem—including planned large annual capacity additions at Inox Clean Energy and external projects executed by parent company Inox Wind—Inox Green said it is firmly on track to exceed 20 GW of serviced capacity in the near future. WWIL’s 4.5 GW Portfolio WWIL’s 4.5 GW O&M portfolio includes a marquee client base comprising the Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy, and Hindustan Zinc. The assets are spread across key wind-rich states, including Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh. The portfolio generated approximately ₹580 crore in revenue in FY26 and benefits from contracted annual price escalation of approximately 5%. Following the transaction, Inox Green’s O&M portfolio stands at approximately 13.3 GWp as of June 2026, inclusive of WWIL’s portfolio and a separate approximately 2 GW wind O&M acquisition currently held as an investment. Inox Green said it expects to leverage operational efficiencies, advanced technology platforms, and group synergies to substantially increase the acquired portfolio’s revenues and operating margins. Commenting on the acquisition, Devansh Jain, Executive Director, INOXGFL Group, said, “This transaction will be a defining step in our strategy to build India’s largest and most technologically advanced renewable energy services platform. Wind World’s quality asset base and deeply entrenched customer relationships complement Inox Green’s strengths and reinforce our long-term growth ambitions. “The transaction substantially enhances our multi-brand OEM O&M capabilities and strengthens our ability to deliver superior operational performance across a larger fleet of wind assets.” Jain added, “We are now focused on a seamless integration of Wind World India’s O&M business, leveraging our combined capabilities to drive greater value for customers, accelerate growth and further consolidate our leadership in the renewable energy services sector.” Akhil Jindal, Group CFO, INOXGFL Group, said, “We are extremely pleased to announce that this milestone transaction has been executed within our disciplined valuation framework. The business has several synergistic opportunities and the transaction multiple works out to approximately 2x EBITDA, based on expected earnings after the full realisation of synergies over the next year. “As we integrate the acquired business, our focus will be on driving operational efficiencies, improving margins and unlocking synergies to maximize value creation.”

stories.headline: Nifty 50 companies likely to log strong double-digit growth in Q2
stories.title: Nifty 50 companies likely to log strong double-digit growth in Q2
stories.summary: Mumbai: Aggregate revenue and net profit of the Nifty 50 companies are expected to grow in double digits year-on-year for the September quarter led by select companies from the automobiles, banking and finance, metals and oil and gas sectors. Revenue and net profit are likely to grow by 19.9% and 22.3% respectively according to the ETIG estimates. Their performance will also benefit from the lower base of 9% and 8.4% growth in revenue and profit in the year-ago quarter."The broader earnings outlook remains healthy, supported by improving domestic demand, strong credit growth, government spending and a recovery in private capex," said Feroze Azeez, Joint CEO, Anand Rathi Wealth.134753222Gautam Duggad, MD and Head of Sales, Institutional Equities, Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) expects Nifty earnings to grow by 27% and that of the companies covered by the broking firm to increase by 22%."Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings for the MOFSL Universe are expected to grow 24% year-on-year during the quarter," Duggad said.Read more: How a 9-year-old Warren Buffett learnt a lesson on compounding by rolling snowballs on the lawn of his Nebraska homeThe operating margin at the aggregate level is likely to contract by a tad 20 basis points to 21.9% from the year ago amid input cost inflation. Azzez expects margins to remain mixed as benefits of lower commodity costs are normalising while wage inflation and higher crude prices are creating some pressure on margins. "For capital goods, infrastructure and manufacturing, margins likely to remain stable to improving, supported by healthy order books, capacity utilisation and operating leverage," he mentioned, adding that for banking and finance companies, earnings growth would be driven more by strong loan growth than by expansion in margins.Read more: Why junk bonds deliver equity-like returns but with far inferior volatility, explains Saurabh MukherjeaDespite near-term challenges in the form of volatile energy prices, geopolitical and tariff risks, and weakening rupee against major currnecies, analysts are optimistic about medium-to-long term growth trajectory. Duggad believes that the risk-reward for Indian equities over a medium and long term has meaningfully improved given healthy earnings growth, resilient macroeconomic environment and cooling valuations. "With earnings growth increasingly concentrated in select themes, we expect market performance to remain firmly bottom-up, favouring growth-oriented businesses that are successfully scaling up and strengthening their competitive positioning," Duggad said. stories.headline: Chief Justice calls for technological sovereignty, justice for farmers
stories.title: Chief Justice calls for technological sovereignty, justice for farmers
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 6: Addressing a special session of the 60th Diamond Jubilee Convention of the Indian Society of Agricultural Engineers (ISAE) at Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), Shalimar, the Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati, called for ensuring that technological advancement in agriculture is accompanied by protection of farmers’ digital, economic and legal rights. The three-day Diamond Jubilee Convention, hosted by SKUAST-K, brought together nearly 700 agricultural engineers, scientists, technocrats and students from India and abroad. The convention focused on themes including ‘Women Leading Engineering Innovations in Smart Farming’ and ‘AI and Robotics for Gen-Z Farming’. “Today, every soldier—whether it be a farmer, a scientist, a teacher, a lawyer, or a judge—will have to be equipped with that kind of technology,” he said, drawing a parallel with the changing nature of modern warfare and the increasing use of drones and other advanced technologies. Earlier, the Chief Justice visited the exhibition stalls set up outside the auditorium and reviewed technologies related to drip irrigation, crop monitoring and drone-based agricultural applications. He stressed the need to make such technologies accessible and understandable to farmers so that they can effectively adopt them. Speaking during the session, Vice Chancellor, Prof Nazir A Ganai SKUAST-K, highlighted the need to accelerate technological interventions in agriculture to unlock the sector’s untapped potential. He said while the Green Revolution helped India overcome food shortages, the country now needs to focus on technology, skilled human resources and innovation to address emerging agricultural challenges. The Vice Chancellor also underlined concerns related to technological and data sovereignty in agriculture, particularly with the increasing use of drones, sensors and digital platforms. He stressed that farmers’ rights must extend beyond markets, land and water to the digital domain as well. The technical sessions featured addresses by Shri N.S. Rathore, Former Vice Chancellor, MPUAT, Udaipur, and Former Deputy Director General (Education), ICAR, on “AI-Driven Agricultural Technology, Smart Skills & Advanced Agricultural Techniques”, and Prof. V.P. Singh, Distinguished Professor, Texas A&M University, USA, on “Mathematical Modelling of the Water-Energy-Environment-Food Nexus.” The session also highlighted the research and innovation ecosystem of SKUAST-K. Over the past five years, the University has generated 148 Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs), including 62 product patents and five global patents, besides supporting 115 student startups and more than 130 commercialised products.

stories.headline: Cabinet celebrates Modi’s 25-year head of Govt run
stories.title: Cabinet celebrates Modi’s 25-year head of Govt run
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister NarendraModi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrated the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of 'Nation First and Citizen First'. The resolution said that three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive LokSabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM NarendraModi. The ten salient features of the resolution capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India. The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India. The resolution said that PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity. The resolution said that PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became Lakhpati Didis, while the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women’s reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded Rs 4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind. The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. The resolution said that his appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. It said that reform emerged as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose. The resolution said that under PM Modi’s leadership, public capital expenditure rose from Rs 2 lakh crore to over Rs 12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around Rs 2 lakh crore to more than Rs 13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs. The resolution said that PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. The resolution said that developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities. The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval. During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. The resolution said that his leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times. It said that 2016 surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot air strikes, and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, 'One Rank One Pension' and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff’s post. It said action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability, and public trust. The resolution links India’s rising stature with PM Modi’s ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union’s G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how India’s capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and India’s growing influence and contribution to shared solutions. The resolution said PM Modi’s vision unites development, cultural confidence, and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarat’s dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham, and Ram Lalla’s consecration strengthened India’s connection with its heritage. The resolution culminated in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant, and developed India by 2047.
